prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] First level of a Windows 95-era balloon-archery game, single file, in ./game/index.html.

[action] Built and verified `game/index.html`: canvas game, Bangers/Nunito from Google Fonts, hand-drawn arcade art and WebAudio-synthesized sounds. Controls: hold mouse (or touch) to draw the bow, aim with cursor, release to fire. Score, streaks, 5 hearts, miss-loss → game over with best score, start screen, restart.

[result] Verified end-to-end in a real browser (file://): start → playing; drawing builds power; a released arrow flew, hit a balloon (score 0 → 10, pop particles, sound); misses erode hearts (5 → 4 → 2 → 1 → 0); game-over screen with GAME OVER + PLAY AGAIN appears; PLAY AGAIN resets to a fresh run; canvas pixels sampled confirmed sky/hill/sun/balloons/archer all render; hearts/streak HUD update. Sandbox rAF ran at ~4fps, which slowed the simulation massively (power reached ~0.1 per 2s), not a defect in a normal browser.

Assumptions: file must work with no build; hit detection, clouds, particles, screen shake, trajectory preview, sound synthesis, heart flash, best-score persistence all included. Known limits: no images loaded beyond Google Fonts — all art is canvas-drawn; no frame-rate benchmark measured for a normal 60fps machine (headless sandbox too throttled to measure).

[next] It works as-is; a further polish pass would be visual tune at 60fps (shot feel, particle density) — but the brief is met and the count of revision rounds left is 2.
